A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RHYTHM study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching appendix sections shifted by the new implementation section.

before.justification: v1 reports original mobility-prediction experiments on three city datasets, alongside model comparisons, ablations and computational measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including prediction scores, temporal analyses, ablations and deployment measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same embeddings, temporal tokenization, hierarchical attention, semantic integration, frozen LLM and output projection. New Algorithm 1 documents this existing pipeline; its inconsistent prompt indexing does not establish an intentional method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Kumamoto, Sapporo and Hiroshima data from YJMob100K. The mobility-prediction task and temporal evaluation scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain LSTM, DeepMove, PatchTST, iTransformer, Time-LLM, CMHSA, PMT, COLA, ST-MoE-BERT and Mobility-LLM. The backbone comparisons, ablation variants and Table 8 deployment comparators also match.

E3.justification: Both retain the 70/20/10 day-based split, 30-minute resolution, 336-slot lookback, 48-slot prediction horizon and segment length, FP16 evaluation and the same metrics. Training settings and appendix experimental configurations are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, daily and weekly analyses, backbone scaling, autoregressive comparison, segment-length sensitivity and pretraining controls are retained. The analyses in v1 Appendices G–I correspond to v3 Appendices H–J; no new test or analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Both report three evaluations with different random seeds and averaged metrics. Table 1 retains the statement that omitted variances are at most 2%, and Table 8 retains the same latency uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerical results and result entries are unchanged, but Table 3 corrects its reported best-result designation for Kumamoto Acc@5. v1 bolds full RHYTHM at 0.5835; v3 instead correctly bolds the variant without trajectory information at 0.5891.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, attention equations, complexity expressions and Section 3.4 theoretical guarantees remain substantively unchanged. Adjusted accents and hidden-state notation are notation corrections; no new theorem, assumption, derivation or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract changes significant sequence shortening to quadratic sequence shortening, a stronger efficiency claim despite unchanged complexity expressions in Section 3.3. It also revises the claimed benefit of freezing to faster training and lower memory usage. The principal contributions and headline empirical claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The introduction adds an explicit language-composition rationale: daily routines form tokens and weekly rhythms form higher-order syntax. This expands the conceptual explanation for using an LLM. Interpretations of the experimental results and the limitations in Section 5 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix E supplies Algorithm 1, organizing semantic precomputation and prediction into explicit pseudocode with inputs, intermediate operations and outputs. This adds procedural documentation rather than demonstrating changed implementation. Hardware, hyperparameters, prompt examples and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and positioning against prior mobility and LLM methods are retained. Reference 43 changes from an ICML entry to an arXiv entry for the same work, which is a bibliographic change rather than changed research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites portions of the introduction, renames the mobility-prediction subsection, standardizes Llama spelling and adds an equal-contribution note. It inserts an implementation appendix and updates subsequent references, while retaining the overall narrative and section organization.

P2.justification: v3 restyles Figure 2, resizes existing figures, corrects Table 3 highlighting and adds the Algorithm 1 display. Tables and text reflow around these changes, but the existing experimental figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added pipeline pseudocode and corrected Table 3 ranking improve accessibility and reporting. However, Algorithm 1 line 4 supplies the full history for every segment prompt, conflicting with the segment-specific equation retained in Section 3.2. The abstract also newly claims quadratic sequence shortening, although Section 3.3 places the quadratic dependence in attention cost. With the empirical evidence unchanged, these documentation gains and newly introduced inconsistencies leave the net quality change unclear.
